title: Do we know what data our employees are entering into third-party AI tools?
description: A board-level oversight question testing whether an organization's generative AI usage policy is technically enforced, rather than a document employees may not follow under time pressure.

history.note: Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources).

question_text: Has management assessed what categories of confidential or proprietary data employees could enter into third-party generative AI tools, and is that policy enforced by a technical control — not just a document employees are expected to remember under time pressure?
rationale: Samsung employees leaked confidential source code and internal notes into ChatGPT within weeks of the tool being permitted, with no technical control in place — showing that policy text alone does not prevent this class of leak.
follow_up_actions: Request the current acceptable-use policy attestation and technical-control configuration.
Ask whether an approved, contractually-protected enterprise-tier AI tool is available as a sanctioned alternative.
Confirm incident response procedures exist for a suspected data leak via a third-party AI tool.

citations.title: Samsung Bans ChatGPT, Google Bard, Other Generative AI Use by Staff After Leak
